title: Data Structure Visualizer website with interactive playground and concept lessons

requirements.text: Create the core site structure for a complete Data Structure Visualizer website with clear navigation: Home, Data Structures, Algorithms, Playground, and About pages.

quotes: i want the complete website of data structure visuvalizer ... it shold be very clear and neat and it should have intractive play ground..

acceptanceCriteria: A top-level navigation is present on all pages and works without reloads.
Each page has a clear header and content area and is responsive on mobile and desktop.

requirements.text: Implement a consistent, neat visual theme (colors, typography, spacing, and component styling) suitable for a student-focused educational tool, and apply it across all pages.

quotes: it shold be very clear and neat

acceptanceCriteria: All pages share the same typography scale, spacing system, and component styling.
Layout remains readable and uncluttered at common breakpoints (mobile/tablet/desktop).

requirements.text: Build a “Concept Lessons” experience for data structures that explains concepts in English using concise text sections and a paired visual demo panel. Include at minimum: Array, Linked List, Stack, Queue, Binary Search Tree, Heap, and Graph.

quotes: to exaplain the concepts of data structues in the visuval form so that students can understand it clearly

acceptanceCriteria: Users can select a data structure and see an overview explanation plus a live visualization panel.
At least the listed data structures have lesson pages/sections with consistent structure (Overview, Operations, Complexity, Common pitfalls).

requirements.text: Create an interactive Playground where students can manipulate a selected data structure and see updates visually. Provide controls for common operations (e.g., insert, delete, search/peek/pop/enqueue/dequeue as relevant), reset, and load a sample scenario.

quotes: it should have intractive play ground..

acceptanceCriteria: Playground supports interactive operations for each implemented data structure type with immediate visual feedback.
Playground provides Reset and Load Sample actions and validates user input (e.g., numeric ranges, required fields).

requirements.text: Add step-by-step animation controls for visualizations: Play/Pause, Step Forward (and optional Step Back where feasible), and Speed control. Ensure operations are understandable (highlight active nodes/indices and show brief operation captions).

quotes: visuval form so that students can understand it clearly

acceptanceCriteria: Users can control animation playback and speed for operations.
Visual state clearly highlights what changed (e.g., compared nodes, moved pointers, swapped elements) with a short caption per step.

requirements.text: Implement algorithm visualizations (at minimum): Sorting (Bubble and Insertion) and Graph Traversal (BFS and DFS) with the same step/animation controls and clear highlighting of active elements.

quotes: data structure visuvalizer ... explain the concepts

acceptanceCriteria: Sorting visualizations show array state changes over time with highlighted comparisons/swaps.
BFS/DFS visualizations show visited order and frontier/stack behavior with node/edge highlighting.

requirements.text: Add a backend content API in the single Motoko actor to serve curated lesson metadata and example presets used by the frontend (e.g., list of topics, per-topic lesson text sections, and sample input sets for the playground).

quotes: complete website of data structure visuvalizer ... explain the concepts ... interactive play ground

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes query methods to list available lessons/topics and fetch lesson details/presets by id.
Frontend loads lesson/preset content via the generated canister actor (no hard dependency on external APIs).

requirements.text: Integrate the frontend with the backend using React Query for loading lesson content and presets, including loading and error UI states.
acceptanceCriteria: Lesson/preset data is fetched through React Query with caching.
Users see clear skeleton/loading states and a readable error message with a retry action when calls fail.

requirements.text: Ensure the UI is accessible and classroom-friendly: keyboard-operable controls, sufficient color contrast, readable font sizes, and clear empty states/tooltips for controls.
acceptanceCriteria: All playground controls are reachable via keyboard and have accessible labels.
Text and key visualization colors meet reasonable contrast and remain understandable without relying on color alone (e.g., add shapes/outlines/labels).

constraints: Do not edit files under the frontend immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT (compose existing UI components instead).
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor; only add migration code if persistent state upgrades are introduced.
nonGoals: User accounts, profiles, or saving progress across devices (unless explicitly requested later).
Integrations with external databases or third-party APIs/services.
Covering every possible data structure/algorithm beyond the minimum set listed in requirements.

required: Minimal academic logo mark with nodes-and-links motif (dsvis-logo.dim_512x512.png)
Wide hero illustration showing abstract data structure shapes (arrays, nodes, tree) in a clean flat style (dsvis-hero.dim_1600x600.png)
